title: STRUT
summary: Rear strut rods (camber rods), all models. A bracket bolts to the underside of the differential carrier with two bolts each side; each strut rod's inner end mounts in that bracket on a camber-adjusting cam bolt with caps on the bushing, and its outer end mounts to the rear spindle support on a shaft secured with a nut and cotter pin. Camber is set by rotating the cam before the nut is torqued at "D" height.

parts.name: CAP
parts.name_expanded: Cap – strut rod inner bushing (both sides)

parts.name: BOLT
parts.name_expanded: Bolt – strut rod bracket to differential carrier

parts.name: BRACKET
parts.name_expanded: Bracket – strut rod (camber) bracket under differential

parts.name: SHAFT
parts.name_expanded: Shaft – strut rod outer mount at spindle support (LH/RH)

fastening.note: Bolts [7] go up from below through lock washer [8], plain washer [9] and the bracket [10] into the differential carrier.

Cam bolt [6] passes through the bracket ear and the strut rod inner bushing with a cap [5] on each side; outer side: cam [3], lock washer [2], nut [1]. NOTE: run nut finger tight, rotate the cam to set camber (Sheet A7), then torque with rear suspension at "D" height.

Shaft [13] passes through the spindle support and the strut rod outer bushing; nut [12] torqued to spec plus extra to line up the cotter pin hole, then cotter pin [11]. The shaft's other end is threaded and sticks out (no separate stud).

notes: NOTE: Assemble nut loosely (finger tight), rotate cam until proper camber is attained (see Sht. A7), then (with rear suspension at "D" height used to set rear geometry) torque nut.
* Plus additional torque to line up C. Pin hole.
